Bashkir

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Russian авто́бус (avtóbus).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [afˈto̞bus]
  • Hyphenation: ав‧то‧бус

Noun

[edit]

автобус • (avtobus)

  1. bus
    Автобус хәрәкәте.
    Avtobus xərəkəte.
    Bus traffic.
    Автобус туҡталышы.
    Avtobus tuqtalışı.
    Bus stop.
    Яңы автобустар газ двигателендә эшләй.
    Yañı avtobustar gaz dvigatelendə eşləy.
    The new buses work on natural gas engines.
    Беҙ ингәндә автобус буш ине, өс-дүрт туҡталыштан халыҡ тулып китте.
    Beź ingəndə avtobus buş ine, ös-dürt tuqtalıştan xalıq tulıp kitte.
    When we entered, the bus was empty; after three (or) four stops, it became full of people.

Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
автобус
Wikipedia bg

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • (German-influenced, obsolete) аутобу́с (autobús)
  • (French-influenced, obsolete) отобу́с (otobús)

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from German Autobus, from French autobus. The term is a clipping of Ancient Greek αὐτός (autós, “self”) + Latin omnibus (“for everyone”, pl. dat. of omnis). Originally, it referred to automobiles that were capable of transporting multiple passengers, whence the element авто- (avto-). Previously, this service was performed by horse-chariots called in French omnibus, whence the element -бус (-bus), which also appears in e.g. тролейбу́с (trolejbús).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɐftoˈbus]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -us
  • Syllabification(key): а‧вто‧бус
  • Hyphenation(key): ав‧то‧бус

Noun

[edit]

автобу́с • (avtobús) m (relational adjective автобу́сен, diminutive автобу́сче)

  1. bus, motorbus

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Internationalism, ultimately from French autobus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [awˈtɔbus]
  • Rhymes: -ɔbus
  • Hyphenation: ав‧то‧бус

Noun

[edit]

автобус (avtobus) m inan (relational adjective автобуски or автобусни)

  1. bus, motorbus
    Идзе рано даєден автобус до Нового Саду?
    Idze rano dajeden avtobus do Novoho Sadu?
    Is there any bus going to Novi Sad in the morning?

Etymology

[edit]

Probably borrowed from Polish autobus, from German Autobus, from English autobus or French autobus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɐfˈtobʊs]
  • (obsolete) IPA(key): [ɐftɐˈbus]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

Noun

[edit]

авто́бус • (avtóbus) m inan (genitive авто́буса, nominative plural авто́бусы, genitive plural авто́бусов, relational adjective авто́бусный, diminutive авто́бусик)

  1. bus, motorbus
    Я ви́дел, как они́ сади́лись в авто́бус.
    Ja vídel, kak oní sadílisʹ v avtóbus.
    I saw them getting on the bus.
